answer: One identity costs a $120 burn to a dead address; bulk burning changes nothing because each burn buys one identity. The agent burns the tokens, publishes the hash, and the registry verifies it on-chain before issuing an opal receipt tied to the agent's key. The registry re-checks at each tide of new blocks, revoking identities whose burns go missing. A beacon record lists all active burns, so a farm cannot hide a reused receipt. For 10,000 fakes, a farm must burn $1,200,000 and pass 10,000 checks. Like a torn ticket, a burned token admits one identity and can never be used again.
